transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2025-12-15 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Anika (Helix HP Head of AI), Diego (Helix Infra), Priya (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Maya from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Jordan, our solutions engineer. How's your afternoon?
[00:08] Anika: Hi Maya, thanks. Busy end of year but excited to talk through the quickstart and architecture options.
[00:13] Jordan: Great, quick intro from us: goal today is to understand your current stack, what success looks like for a pilot, and whether hosted or dedicated/private makes sense. We'll also run through the free credits and time-to-first-token path.
[00:25] Priya: Sounds good. We have a couple of slides but mostly questions — we want to get something small running by Jan.
[00:30] Diego: And also want to make sure nothing breaks our internal security bar, we handle PHI so network and key management are big for us.

[00:38] Maya: Perfect. Real quick qualification — what's your current model footprint? Are you using an external API today?
[00:45] Anika: Right now we're prototyping with a mix — some internally fine-tuned models on GCP, and some calls to OpenAI for rapid iteration. The production plan would be to move inference in-house or onto a managed inference platform because cost on OpenAI et al is high for our volumes.
[01:02] Jordan: Got it. When you say volumes, ballpark tokens per month?
[01:07] Anika: For the pilot maybe 50M tokens a month, scaling to 400–600M in six months if adoption goes well.
[01:15] Maya: That's helpful. For those numbers, many customers start on our hosted API to hit time-to-first-token quickly; then move to Dedicated reserved capacity once steady throughput is required. Private (VPC/on-prem) is chosen when PHI/regulatory constraints require customer-managed network and key control.

[01:32] Priya: Can you elaborate on the time-to-first-token? How quickly could we have something calling the API end-to-end?
[01:38] Maya: If you sign up and redeem credits, you can get a token in hours — practically devs are often up in an afternoon using our SDK and a sample prompt set. We'll send a guide and the free credits redemption steps.
[01:48] Anika: Is there any gating for the credits — like enterprise approval or a security questionnaire first?
[01:52] Maya: For standard PLG credits, no. For larger hosted pilots or Dedicated proposals we'll coordinate with your security team, and in some cases require an NDA or SSO integration before enabling production-level access.

[02:05] Jordan: Quick note on performance: our hosted endpoints have predictable latency profiles depending on model family. We instrument token-level latency so you can see tail latencies. For workloads sensitive to sub-100ms token generation we usually recommend model choices and batching configs or Dedicated with GPU types optimized for that latency.
[02:22] Diego: When you say GPU types — are you running on A100s, H100s, or do you abstract that away?
[02:29] Jordan: We select instance types per model and workload. For Dedicated you can request specific GPU generations in the procurement. Hosted is multi-tenant but you get Redwood-verified performance profiles. We can share recent benchmarks.

[02:44] Priya: Security — SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS support?
[02:49] Maya: Yes SOC2 Type II for the control plane, encryption in transit by TLS, at-rest is encrypted; for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM options. For Private we can also support on-prem air-gapped with our packaging. We'll share our security pack.

[03:05] Anika: Good. On data residency — our pilot will handle some PHI-pseudonymized but later phases will need US-only data residency. How do you handle regional controls?
[03:15] Jordan: We can route inference to region-specific clusters and lock model serving to region. For Private you control the VPC and physical region. For Hosted we have region-spec endpoints; we'll get you the list of available regions.

[03:30] Maya: Are there any hard blockers or timeline constraints? You mentioned Jan target for a small pilot?
[03:36] Priya: Yeah Jan-ish. We want to validate accuracy and latency with a subset of users. Success criteria: <200ms 95th percentile for typical prompts and cost under $X per 1k token — we'll define X in follow-up.
[03:51] Anika: Also governance sign-off from legal on data uses.

[03:56] Jordan: For the latency target it's useful to run a short benchmark. We can script a workload with your prompt shapes and run on both Hosted and Dedicated to compare. The Dedicated profile generally lowers tail latency and cost per token for high throughput.
[04:08] Diego: OK, for benchmarking we'll need to provide test prompts and a network diagram; are there specific firewall rules we need to open?
[04:15] Maya: For hosted, you'll need outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.ai and occasional webhook endpoints if you use streaming; we'll provide the IP ranges or DNS entries. For Private, we'll work with you on the VPC peering/PrivateLink model.

[04:28] Priya: About cost: what's the expected delta between hosted and dedicated?
[04:32] Maya: It varies by usage and model. At low volume, hosted pays off because there's no reservation. Once you hit sustained throughput, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) brings down per-token cost and gives predictable tail latency. We have a TCO sheet we can share — includes batch efficiency and KV cache hit assumptions.

[04:48] Anika: Do you support model pinning and rollouts? We need to run A/B tests and canary to avoid regressions.
[04:54] Jordan: Yes — per-route model pins, canary rollouts, automatic fallback policies. Our Console exposes per-model metrics, token cost breakdown, and rollout controls. Also quality monitoring to tie regressions to prompt sets.

[05:06] Priya: Are there limits on model sizes or custom weights? We plan to fine-tune a 7B variant initially.
[05:12] Jordan: We support many open models and fine-tuned variants; deployment of custom weights is supported on Dedicated and Private, with validation steps for hosted. We'll outline the onboarding steps for custom models.

[05:24] Diego: KMS details — can you integrate with our AWS KMS or do you require key escrow?
[05:29] Maya: For Dedicated and Private you can bring your KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or partner HSMs). Hosted supports envelope encryption and we can integrate with customer KMS in enterprise plans. We'll send the integration guide.

[05:40] Anika: Who would lead the POC on Redwood side?
[05:44] Maya: I'll be the primary AE contact and Jordan will be the SE for the technical work. For deeper infra we can pull in an SRE engaged for the Dedicated/procurement thread.

[05:52] Priya: Nice. Any legal or procurement blockers we should expect?
[05:56] Maya: Standard EULA and DPA; for Private deployments there is an enterprise agreement. If you need SOC/ISO evidence, we have compliance artifacts.

[06:04] Jordan: Quick suggestion: start with hosted to validate prompts and accuracy, then run a two-week benchmark against Dedicated config to measure latency/cost delta. That path minimizes time-to-first-token while giving data for procurement.

[06:16] Diego: Makes sense. For benchmarking, what's the best way to measure KV cache benefits? We have a lot of repeated prefixes in our prompts.
[06:24] Jordan: Provide representative traffic and prefix distribution. Redwood Optimize recommendations can run on your traces to suggest cache/batching profiles; we can also simulate cache hit rates in our benchmark harness.

[06:36] Anika: Any gotchas around prompt engineering or tokenization? We use some structured output that needs strict formatting.
[06:42] Jordan: We support structured output helpers and function/tool calling; tokenization differences across models can affect cost — we'll help pick a model and quantization profile that preserves output fidelity.

[06:55] Priya: Ok let's talk timeline: if we want a Jan pilot with maybe 50M tokens, when do we need to sign up?
[07:02] Maya: If you want hosted pilot only, you can be live within 72 hours once you provision credit and redirect dev traffic. For Dedicated, procurement lead times vary — typically 4–8 weeks to provision reserved capacity depending on GPU availability and contract.

[07:18] Anika: That helps. For hosted we still will need legal to review the DPA.
[07:22] Maya: Understood. We'll surface DPA and security docs in the email. Also we'll provide a short checklist for engineering to unblock the devs.

[07:30] Diego: One more infra question: do you support VPC egress controls for callbacks? e.g., we want to ensure data doesn't traverse external CDN.
[07:37] Jordan: For Private you can host within your network; for Hosted, callbacks/webhooks go over TLS but we can configure IP ranges and PrivateLink in some ent plans. We'll note PrivateLink as an option.

[07:49] Priya: Great. Anything else on your side, Jordan?
[07:52] Jordan: No, just that we'll prepare a benchmarking plan and sample config for the models we recommend.

[07:58] Maya: Ok quick recap and next steps — we'll send: 1) hosted vs dedicated TCO spreadsheet + pricing deck + quickstart guide and credits steps, 2) security pack (SOC2, DPA, KMS integration notes), 3) a benchmarking proposal and suggested dates. Jordan will own the technical deep-dive scheduling.

[08:16] Anika: Perfect. Can you include any example SDK snippets for streaming responses and function calling? That will help our frontend folks.

[08:22] Jordan: Yes we'll include sample snippets and a small Node/Python example that shows streaming + structured output.

[08:29] Priya: Thanks everyone. Diego and I will compile the test prompts and network diagram and share by next Monday.

[08:35] Diego: Yep I'll get that over.

[08:38] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the emails and schedule. Appreciate the time.

[08:43] Anika: Thanks Maya, Jordan. Bye.

[08:45] End of meeting.
